title: Postman local data
whyItMatters: Postman keeps local collections, environments and request history here. Environment variables often contain API keys and access tokens, and the history shows every endpoint the person called.
source: Postman Support, How to remove local data: the Postman folder is in ~/Library/Application Support on macOS - https://support.postman.com/hc/en-us/articles/4410785125271-How-to-remove-local-data
notes: Holds collections, environments, request history and the sign-in state. Contents are not read.

cleanup.exportFirst: Export the collections and environments you need from Postman, and keep any API keys from environment variables somewhere safe.
cleanup.signOut: Sign out of Postman in the app, then remove this device from the account's sessions on the Postman website.
steps: Export the collections and environments you want to keep.
Sign out of Postman and quit the app.
Uninstall Postman by moving it to the Trash.
Delete the folder named in the plan, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes local collections, environments, request history and the sign-in state from this Mac. Anything already synced stays in the Postman account.
cleanup.source: Postman Support, How to remove local data: https://support.postman.com/hc/en-us/articles/4410785125271-How-to-remove-local-data
